answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy can require every trader to hold an opal credential earned by one bonded job: the agent verifies an invoice while staking a deposit that a panel of established peers can slash if the work is fake. Each job is signed with the agent's own quill, its private key, so one operator cannot sign for a hundred puppets without staking a hundred deposits. A raven courier with no stake in the outcome carries the verdict to the ledger, so no single witness can bury a bad result. Forging an army costs money per identity, while an honest newcomer needs just one honest job.
